chapters.title: Love Righteousness
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 1

1Love righteousness, you who judge the earth;
think of the Lord with goodness,
and seek Him in simplicity of heart,

2for He is found by those who do not test Him,
and shows Himself to those who do not distrust Him.

3For crooked thoughts separate from God,
and His power, when it is tested, exposes the foolish.

4Wisdom will not enter a soul that plots evil,
nor dwell in a body in debt to sin.

5For the holy spirit of discipline flees deceit,
and rises and leaves foolish thoughts,
and is put to shame when wrongdoing draws near.

6For wisdom is a spirit that loves mankind,
and will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his words,
because God is witness of his inmost being,
a true overseer of his heart,
and a hearer of his tongue.

7For the Spirit of the Lord has filled the world,
and that which holds all things together
knows every voice.

8Therefore no one who speaks what is unrighteous will escape notice,
and justice, when it convicts, will not pass him by.

9For inquiry will be made into the plans of the ungodly,
and the report of his words will come to the Lord
to convict him of his lawless deeds;

10for a jealous ear hears all things,
and the murmur of grumbling is not hidden.

11Beware, then, of useless grumbling,
and keep your tongue from slander;
for no secret word goes for nothing,
and a lying mouth kills the soul.

12Do not seek death by the error of your life,
nor bring on destruction by the works of your hands;

13for God did not make death,
and He takes no delight in the destruction of the living.

14For He created all things that they might exist,
and the things that come into being in the world are wholesome;
there is no poison of destruction in them,
and the kingdom of Hades is not on earth.

15For righteousness is immortal.

16But the ungodly summoned death by their hands and their words;
thinking him a friend, they pined for him,
and made a covenant with him,
because they are fit to belong to his party.

Notes

  • v1 "Love righteousness, you who judge the earth" — rendered from the Greek, in which the book was written; Swete's text, verse numbers as the English. The book speaks in the voice of the king who prayed for wisdom (9:7–8; 1 Kings 3:9), though it never gives his name. It opens by calling to rulers, as Psalm 2:10 does: Now therefore, kings, be wise; be warned, judges of the earth, where the Greek has the same hoi krinontes tēn gēn.

  • v5 "the holy spirit of discipline" — hagion pneuma paideias: the spirit of wisdom (v6, "wisdom is a spirit"), set in lowercase since it is not named "of God" or "of the Lord." "Discipline" is paideia, the Greek Proverbs' word for musar, "discipline" (Proverbs 1:2, 7).

  • v6 "a spirit that loves mankind" — philanthrōpon, the word behind "philanthropy." "His inmost being" — literally "his kidneys," the seat of feeling beside the heart (Psalm 7:9; Jeremiah 17:10).

  • v7 "the Spirit of the Lord… that which holds all things together" — to synechon ta panta, neuter, the power that keeps the world from falling apart. Paul says the same of Christ with a related verb: in Him all things hold together (Colossians 1:17).

  • vv13–14 "God did not make death… He created all things that they might exist" — death is no part of the world God made; the next chapter says how it came in (2:24).

  • v16 "made a covenant with him" — synthēkē, the word of Isaiah 28:15 in the Greek: we have made a covenant with Hades, and an agreement with death. "Death" in the first line names the "him" of the Greek.

chapters.title: The Reasoning of the Ungodly
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 2

1For they reasoned unsoundly, saying to themselves:
"Short and sorrowful is our life,
and there is no remedy when a man comes to his end,
and no one has been known to return from Hades.

2For we were born by chance,
and afterward we shall be as though we had never been;
for the breath in our nostrils is smoke,
and reason is a spark at the beating of our hearts;

3when it is put out, the body will turn to ashes,
and the spirit will dissolve like empty air.

4Our name will be forgotten in time,
and no one will remember our works;
our life will pass away like the traces of a cloud,
and be scattered like mist
chased by the rays of the sun
and weighed down by its heat.

5For our life is the passing of a shadow,
and there is no turning back from our end,
because it is sealed, and no one returns.

6Come, then, let us enjoy the good things that are here,
and make use of the creation eagerly, as in youth.

7Let us take our fill of costly wine and perfumes,
and let no flower of the air pass us by.

8Let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.

9Let none of us go without a share in our revelry;
everywhere let us leave signs of our merriment,
because this is our portion, and this our lot.

10Let us oppress the righteous poor man;
let us not spare the widow,
nor respect the gray hair of the aged, grown old in years.

11But let our strength be our law of righteousness,
for what is weak proves itself useless.

12Let us lie in wait for the righteous man,
because he is a nuisance to us and opposes our actions;
he reproaches us for sins against the law,
and charges us with sins against our upbringing.

13He professes to have knowledge of God,
and calls himself a child of the Lord.

14He has become a reproof of our thoughts;
even the sight of him is a burden to us,

15because his life is unlike the life of others,
and his ways are strange.

16We are counted by him as counterfeit,
and he keeps away from our ways as from uncleanness;
he calls the end of the righteous happy,
and boasts that God is his father.

17Let us see if his words are true,
and let us test what will happen at his end.

18For if the righteous man is God's son, He will help him,
and rescue him from the hand of his adversaries.

19Let us test him with insult and torture,
so that we may learn how gentle he is,
and put his patience to the proof.

20Let us condemn him to a shameful death,
for, by his own words, he will be watched over."

21So they reasoned, and they went astray,
for their wickedness blinded them,

22and they did not know the mysteries of God,
nor hope for the wages of holiness,
nor discern the prize for blameless souls;

23for God created man for incorruption,
and made him the image of His own nature,

24but through the envy of the devil death entered the world,
and those who belong to his party experience it.

Notes

  • vv1–9 "Short and sorrowful is our life" — the ungodly speak like the Preacher read with God left out: this is our portion (Ecclesiastes 9:9), eat your bread with joy (9:7). The Preacher ends know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment (11:9); these men end in vv10–20.

  • v7 "flower of the air" — anthos aeros: the bloom of the season, carried on the air, which they mean to pick before it passes.

  • v12 "he is a nuisance to us" — dyschrēstos, the word of the Greek of Isaiah 3:10: Let us bind the righteous man, for he is a nuisance to us. The plot of vv12–20 grows from that verse.

  • v13 "a child of the Lord" — pais Kyriou: pais is a child or a servant. It is the word of the Greek of Isaiah 52:13, my servant (pais) shall understand, and v16 ("God is his father") and v18 ("God's son") take it as "child."

  • vv17–18 "if the righteous man is God's son, He will help him, and rescue him" — the mockers at the cross speak these words: He trusts in God; let God rescue Him now, if He wants Him. For He said, "I am the Son of God" (Matthew 27:43).

  • v23 "the image of His own nature" — eikona tēs idias idiotētos: God's own selfhood, the image of Genesis 1:27 given to man for incorruption.

  • v24 "through the envy of the devil death entered the world" — diabolos, "the slanderer," the word the Greek uses for the satan of Job 1:6. Paul's through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin (Romans 5:12) uses the same "entered into the world."

chapters.title: The Souls of the Righteous
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 3

1But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God,
and no torment will touch them.

2In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died,
and their departure was thought to be an affliction,

3and their going from us to be their ruin;
but they are at peace.

4For though in the sight of men they were punished,
their hope is full of immortality.

5Having been disciplined a little, they will receive great good,
because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself;

6like gold in the furnace He tried them,
and like a whole burnt offering He accepted them.

7In the time of their visitation they will shine out,
and will run like sparks through the stubble.

8They will judge nations and rule over peoples,
and the Lord will reign over them forever.

9Those who trust in Him will understand truth,
and the faithful will stay with Him in love,
because grace and mercy are with His chosen ones.

10But the ungodly will be punished as their reasoning deserves,
those who neglected the righteous man and rebelled against the Lord;

11for whoever despises wisdom and discipline is miserable.
Their hope is empty, their labors unprofitable,
and their works useless.

12Their wives are foolish, and their children evil;
their offspring are accursed.

13For blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled,
who has not known a sinful bed;
she will have fruit at the visitation of souls.

14So too the eunuch whose hand has done no lawless deed,
and who has not plotted wicked things against the Lord;
for a special favor will be given him for his faithfulness,
and a share in the temple of the Lord more pleasing to the heart.

15For the fruit of good labors is glorious,
and the root of understanding does not fail.

16But the children of adulterers will not come to maturity,
and the offspring of an unlawful bed will vanish.

17Even if they live long, they will be counted as nothing,
and at the last their old age will be without honor.

18If they die early, they have no hope,
and no comfort on the day of decision.

19For the end of an unrighteous generation is grievous.

Notes

  • v1 "the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God" — the answer to 2:1–20: the righteous man whom the ungodly killed to see whether God would help him is safe in God's hand.

  • vv5–6 "disciplined… tested… like gold in the furnace" — paideuthentes, from paideia, "discipline" (1:5); the refining of Proverbs 17:3, the crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests hearts.

  • v7 "they will shine out" — compare Daniel 12:3, those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the expanse. "Like sparks through the stubble" — fire that runs through a dry field.

  • v11 "whoever despises wisdom and discipline" — Proverbs 1:7 in the Greek, the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline, with the same verb (exouthenein).

  • vv13–14 "the barren woman… the eunuch" — the two who had no children, and whom Isaiah comforts: Sing, barren one (54:1), and the eunuchs who keep God's covenant, to whom He gives in My house and within My walls a monument and a name better than sons and daughters (56:3–5).

  • v13 "the visitation of souls" — episkopē, God's coming to look upon and judge, as in v7 ("the time of their visitation").

chapters.title: The Righteous Who Die Young
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 4

1Better is childlessness with virtue,
for in the memory of virtue is immortality,
because it is known both by God and by men.

2When it is present, people imitate it,
and they long for it when it has gone;
and through all time it marches in triumph, wearing a crown,
having won the contest for prizes that are undefiled.

3But the many children of the ungodly will be of no use;
from bastard slips they will not strike deep roots
or take a firm hold.

4For even if they put forth branches for a while,
standing unsteadily they will be shaken by the wind,
and by the violence of the winds they will be uprooted.

5The branches will be broken off before they come to maturity,
and their fruit will be useless,
not ripe enough to eat, and good for nothing.

6For children born of unlawful unions
are witnesses of evil against their parents when they are examined.

7But the righteous man, though he die early, will be at rest.

8For old age is not honored for length of time,
nor measured by number of years;

9but understanding is gray hair for men,
and a spotless life is ripe old age.

10Having pleased God, he was loved by Him,
and while living among sinners he was taken up.

11He was caught away so that evil might not change his understanding,
or deceit beguile his soul.

12For the spell of worthlessness obscures what is good,
and the roving of desire undermines an innocent mind.

13Made perfect in a short time,
he fulfilled long years;

14for his soul was pleasing to the Lord;
therefore He took him quickly from the wickedness around him.
But the peoples saw and did not understand,
nor take such a thing to heart,

15that grace and mercy are with His chosen ones,
and that He watches over His holy ones.

16The righteous man who has died will condemn the ungodly who are living,
and youth quickly made perfect will condemn the long old age of the unrighteous.

17For they will see the end of the wise man,
and will not understand what the Lord purposed for him,
and for what end He kept him safe.

18They will see, and will despise him,
but the Lord will laugh them to scorn.

19After this they will become a dishonored corpse,
and an outrage among the dead forever,
for He will dash them speechless and headlong,
and shake them from their foundations;
they will be left utterly dry and barren,
and they will be in anguish,
and the memory of them will perish.

20They will come with dread when their sins are counted up,
and their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.

Notes

  • v10 "Having pleased God… he was taken up" — the words of Enoch in the Greek of Genesis 5:24: Enoch pleased God… because God took him up (euarestein, metatithenai). The book does not name him; it makes his story the pattern for every righteous person who dies young. Hebrews 11:5 uses the same two verbs of Enoch.

  • v11 "He was caught away" — hērpagē, the verb of a sudden snatching away (1 Thessalonians 4:17, we… shall be caught up).

  • v12 "the spell of worthlessness" — baskania, the evil eye, a bewitching glance that darkens what is good.

  • vv13–14 "Made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years" — a short life can be a full one; the measure is not years (vv8–9).

  • v15 — the line of 3:9, "grace and mercy are with His chosen ones," now with God's watching over His holy ones.

  • v18 "the Lord will laugh them to scorn" — ekgelasetai, the verb of the Greek of Psalm 2:4, He who sits in the heavens will laugh at them.

  • v19 "dash them speechless and headlong" — prēneis, face down: the fall of those who mocked the righteous (2:17–20).

chapters.title: The Righteous Man Will Stand
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 5

1Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness
to face those who afflicted him
and made light of his labors.

2When they see him, they will be shaken with dreadful fear,
and they will be amazed at his unexpected salvation.

3They will say to themselves, repenting,
and groaning in anguish of spirit:
"This is the man whom we once held in derision
and made a byword of reproach —

4we fools! We counted his life madness,
and his end without honor.

5How has he been numbered among the sons of God,
and how is his lot among the holy ones?

6So we strayed from the way of truth,
and the light of righteousness did not shine on us,
and the sun did not rise on us.

7We took our fill of the paths of lawlessness and destruction,
and we journeyed through trackless deserts,
but the way of the Lord we did not know.

8What has our arrogance profited us?
What good has wealth with boasting brought us?

9All those things have passed away like a shadow,
and like a rumor that hurries by;

10like a ship that passes through the surging water,
and when it has gone by no trace can be found,
nor the track of its keel in the waves;

11or as, when a bird flies through the air,
no sign of its passage is found,
but the light air, lashed by the beat of its wings
and torn by the force of its rushing,
is passed through by the moving of its wings,
and afterward no sign of its coming is found there;

12or as, when an arrow is shot at a target,
the air, divided, at once comes back together,
so that no one knows its path.

13So we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be;
we had no sign of virtue to show,
but were consumed in our wickedness."

14For the hope of the ungodly man is like chaff carried by the wind,
and like a light frost driven away by a storm;
it is scattered like smoke by the wind,
and it passes like the remembrance of a guest who stays one day.

15But the righteous live forever,
and their reward is with the Lord,
and the Most High takes care of them.

16Therefore they will receive the glorious kingdom
and the crown of beauty from the hand of the Lord,
because with His right hand He will cover them,
and with His arm He will shield them.

17He will take His zeal as His full armor,
and will arm creation to repel His enemies;

18He will put on righteousness as a breastplate,
and wear impartial judgment as a helmet;

19He will take holiness as an invincible shield,

20and sharpen stern wrath for a sword,
and the world will fight with Him against the senseless.

21Well-aimed shafts of lightning will fly,
and from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow,
they will leap to the mark,

22and hailstones full of wrath will be hurled as from a catapult;
the water of the sea will rage against them,
and rivers will relentlessly overwhelm them;

23a mighty wind will rise against them,
and like a whirlwind it will winnow them away.
Lawlessness will lay waste the whole earth,
and evildoing will overturn the thrones of rulers.

Notes

  • v1 "Then the righteous man will stand" — the judgment scene answering 2:12–20: the man the ungodly tested to death now faces them, and they speak again (vv3–13), this time in regret.

  • v5 "among the sons of God… among the holy ones" — the company of heaven, the "sons of God" of Job 38:7; he whom they mocked for calling God his father (2:16) is counted with them.

  • v6 "the sun did not rise on us" — the sun of righteousness that rises for those who fear God's name (Malachi 4:2).

  • vv9–12 "a ship… a bird… an arrow" — three things that pass and leave no trace, like the sayings of Reproof 6:19 (Proverbs 30:19), the way of an eagle in the sky… the way of a ship on the high seas.

  • v14 "a guest who stays one day" — remembered for a day and gone.

  • vv17–20 "full armor… breastplate… helmet… shield… sword" — God armed for battle, as in Isaiah 59:17, He put on righteousness as a breastplate. Paul gives the same armor to believers: the full armor (panoplia) of God, the breastplate of righteousness (Ephesians 6:11–17).

  • vv20–22 "the world will fight with Him" — lightning, hail, sea and rivers take God's side against the wicked; the book returns to this in the plagues of Egypt and the sea (16:17; 19:6).

  • v23 "a mighty wind" — pneuma dynameōs, a wind of power: the storm of vv21–22, lowercase.

or as, when an arrow is shot at a target, the air, divided, at once comes back together, so that no one knows its path.
So we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be; we had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness."

chapters.title: Listen, Kings
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 6

1Listen, then, kings, and understand;
learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.

2Give ear, you who rule over multitudes
and pride yourselves on crowds of nations.

3For your dominion was given you by the Lord,
and your sovereignty by the Most High,
who will examine your works and search out your plans.

4Because, as servants of His kingdom, you did not judge rightly,
nor keep the law,
nor walk according to the purpose of God,

5He will come upon you terribly and swiftly,
because severe judgment falls on those in high places.

6For the lowliest may be pardoned in mercy,
but the mighty will be mightily tested.

7For the Master of all will not show partiality,
nor stand in awe of greatness,
because He Himself made both small and great,
and He cares for all alike;

8but a strict inquiry is in store for the mighty.

9To you, then, monarchs, my words are directed,
so that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.

10For those who keep holy things in holiness will be made holy,
and those who have been taught them will find a defense.

11So set your desire on my words;
long for them, and you will be instructed.

12Wisdom is radiant and unfading,
and she is easily seen by those who love her.

13She is quick to make herself known to those who desire her.

14He who rises early for her will not grow weary,
for he will find her sitting at his gates.

15To think about her is the perfection of understanding,
and he who lies awake for her sake will soon be free from care,

16because she goes about seeking those worthy of her,
and graciously shows herself to them on their paths,
and meets them in every thought.

17For her truest beginning is the desire for discipline,

18and care for discipline is love,
and love is the keeping of her laws,
and attention to her laws is the assurance of incorruption,

19and incorruption brings one near to God;

20so the desire for wisdom leads to a kingdom.

21If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, monarchs of the peoples,
honor wisdom, so that you may reign forever.

22What wisdom is, and how she came to be, I will tell you,
and I will not hide mysteries from you,
but I will trace her out from the beginning of her coming to be,
and make the knowledge of her plain,
and I will not pass by the truth;

23nor will I travel in the company of wasting envy,
for such a man will have no share in wisdom.

24A multitude of wise men is the salvation of the world,
and a sensible king is the stability of his people.

25Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will profit.

Notes

  • v1 "Listen, then, kings" — the call of 1:1 to "you who judge the earth," taken up again before the book turns to wisdom herself.

  • v3 "your dominion was given you by the Lord" — as Paul says, there is no authority except from God (Romans 13:1), and Jesus to Pilate, you would have no authority over Me at all unless it had been given you from above (John 19:11).

  • v6 "the mighty will be mightily tested" — dynatoi dynatōs, the word doubled: the greater the power, the stricter the account (compare Luke 12:48).

  • v7 "will not show partiality" — literally "will not shrink back before a face"; compare Deuteronomy 10:17, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe. "He Himself made both small and great" — as the LORD is the Maker of them all (Proverbs 22:2).

  • v9 "monarchs" — tyrannoi, rulers who hold power alone; the word names the office, not cruelty, and stands beside "kings" and "judges" (vv1–2).

  • v10 "keep holy things in holiness will be made holy" — hosiōs ta hosia hosiōthēsontai, one root three times.

  • v14 "he will find her sitting at his gates" — Proverbs 8:34 blesses the one watching daily at my gates; here wisdom sits at the seeker's gate before he wakes.

  • vv17–20 — a chain in which each step takes up the last word of the one before: desire for discipline, care for discipline, love, keeping her laws, incorruption, nearness to God, and so to a kingdom.

  • v24 "the salvation of the world" — sōtēria, the word of the Greek of Proverbs 11:14, in an abundance of counselors there is victory.

chapters.title: A Reflection of Eternal Light
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 7

1I also am mortal, like everyone,
a descendant of the first-formed man, born of the earth;
and in my mother's womb I was molded into flesh,

2within the time of ten months,
compacted in blood from the seed of a man
and the pleasure that comes with sleep.

3When I was born, I too drew in the common air,
and fell upon the earth that we all share,
and my first sound was a cry, like that of all.

4I was nursed in swaddling cloths, and with cares.

5For no king has had any other beginning of existence;

6there is one entrance into life for all,
and one way out alike.

7Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me;
I called, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

8I preferred her to scepters and thrones,
and I counted wealth as nothing beside her.

9Nor did I liken to her any priceless stone,
because all gold is a little sand in her sight,
and silver will be counted as clay before her.

10I loved her more than health and beauty,
and chose to have her rather than light,
because her radiance never sleeps.

11All good things came to me together with her,
and countless wealth in her hands.

12I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom leads them,
but I did not know that she was their source.

13I learned without guile and I share without grudging;
I do not hide her wealth.

14For she is an unfailing treasure for men;
those who use it gain friendship with God,
commended to Him by the gifts that come from discipline.

15May God grant me to speak with judgment,
and to think thoughts worthy of what has been given,
for He is the guide even of wisdom
and the corrector of the wise.

16For both we and our words are in His hand,
and all understanding and skill in crafts.

17For it is He who gave me unerring knowledge of what exists,
to know the structure of the world and the working of the elements;

18the beginning and end and middle of times,
the turns of the solstices and the changes of the seasons,

19the cycles of the year and the positions of the stars,

20the natures of living creatures and the tempers of wild beasts,
the forces of winds and the reasonings of men,
the varieties of plants and the powers of roots.

21I learned both what is hidden and what is plain,

22for wisdom, the fashioner of all things, taught me.
For in her is a spirit that is intelligent, holy,
unique, manifold, subtle,
mobile, clear, unpolluted,
distinct, invulnerable, loving the good, keen,
unhindered, beneficent,

23loving mankind, steadfast, sure, free from care,
all-powerful, overseeing all,
and passing through all spirits
that are intelligent, pure and most subtle.

24For wisdom is more mobile than any motion;
because of her pureness she pervades and passes through all things.

25For she is a breath of the power of God,
and a pure outflowing of the glory of the Almighty;
therefore nothing defiled finds its way into her.

26For she is a reflection of eternal light,
a spotless mirror of the working of God,
and an image of His goodness.

27Though she is one, she can do all things,
and while remaining in herself, she makes all things new;
in every generation she passes into holy souls
and makes them friends of God and prophets;

28for God loves nothing so much as the one who lives with wisdom.

29For she is more beautiful than the sun,
and excels every constellation of the stars;
compared with light she is found to be superior,

30for night follows the light,
but against wisdom evil does not prevail.

Notes

  • vv1–6 "I also am mortal" — the king begins as every person begins: from Adam, "the first-formed man, born of the earth" (Genesis 2:7), carried in the womb "ten months" counted by the moon, crying at birth. What he has, he received by asking (v7).

  • v7 "Therefore I prayed" — Solomon's request at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:5–12); the prayer itself comes in chapter 9.

  • vv8–11 "I preferred her to scepters and thrones" — the choice of 1 Kings 3:11–13, and the riches that came with it unasked; compare Proverbs 8:10–11 and Job 28:15–19.

  • v20 "the forces of winds" — pneumatōn, winds or spirits; in this list of the natural world it is the winds. The list matches what Solomon spoke of in 1 Kings 4:33: trees, beasts, birds, creeping things and fish.

  • v22 "the fashioner of all things" — technitis, a craftswoman: Proverbs 8:30, I was beside Him as a master workman. "Unique" — monogenes, "the only one of its kind," the word John uses of the Son (John 1:14, 18; 3:16). The spirit in wisdom is given twenty-one marks, three times seven.

  • v25 "a breath… a pure outflowing" — atmis, vapor, and aporroia, what streams out from a source: wisdom comes from God as breath from a mouth.

  • v26 "a reflection of eternal light… an image of His goodness" — apaugasma and eikōn. Hebrews says the Son is the radiance (apaugasma) of His glory (Hebrews 1:3), and Paul, the image (eikōn) of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15).

  • v27 "friends of God and prophets" — Abraham is called God's friend (2 Chronicles 20:7; James 2:23).

  • v30 "against wisdom evil does not prevail" — compare John 1:5, the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

chapters.title: I Sought Her for My Bride
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 8

1She reaches mightily from one end to the other,
and she orders all things well.

2I loved her and sought her from my youth;
I desired to take her for my bride,
and I became a lover of her beauty.

3She glorifies her noble birth by living with God,
and the Master of all loved her.

4For she is an initiate in the knowledge of God,
and the one who chooses His works.

5If riches are a desirable possession in life,
what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?

6If understanding is at work,
who more than she is the fashioner of what exists?

7If anyone loves righteousness,
her labors are virtues;
for she teaches self-control and understanding,
righteousness and courage;
nothing in life is more useful for men than these.

8If anyone longs for wide experience,
she knows the things of old, and infers the things to come;
she understands turns of speech and the answers to riddles;
she knows beforehand signs and wonders,
and the outcomes of seasons and times.

9Therefore I resolved to take her to live with me,
knowing that she would give me good counsel,
and encouragement in cares and grief.

10Because of her I shall have glory among the crowds
and honor before the elders, though I am young.

11I shall be found keen in judgment,
and in the sight of rulers I shall be admired.

12When I am silent they will wait for me,
and when I speak they will pay attention;
and if I speak at length,
they will put their hands on their mouths.

13Because of her I shall have immortality,
and leave an everlasting memory to those who come after me.

14I shall govern peoples,
and nations will be subject to me;

15dread monarchs will be afraid when they hear of me;
among the people I shall show myself good,
and in war courageous.

16When I come into my house, I shall find rest with her,
for companionship with her has no bitterness,
and life with her has no pain,
but gladness and joy.

17When I had considered these things within myself,
and pondered in my heart
that in kinship with wisdom there is immortality,

18and in friendship with her pure delight,
and in the labors of her hands unfailing wealth,
and in the practice of her company understanding,
and renown in sharing her words,
I went about seeking how to take her for my own.

19As a child I was gifted by nature,
and a good soul fell to my lot;

20or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.

21But I knew that I would not possess her unless God gave her —
and it was a mark of understanding to know whose gift she was —
so I appealed to the Lord and entreated Him,
and with my whole heart I said:

Notes

  • v1 "She reaches mightily from one end to the other" — the close of 7:22–30: wisdom passes through all things and sets them in order, diatenei… dioikei, "she stretches… she governs."

  • v2 "to take her for my bride" — wisdom as the wife a young man should seek, as in Proverbs 4:6–9 and 7:4, Say to wisdom, "You are my sister."

  • vv3, 9, 16 "living with God… to live with me… life with her" — symbiōsis, "living together," each time: she shares God's life, and the king wants her to share his.

  • v4 "an initiate in the knowledge of God" — mystis, one admitted to secret rites: she knows God's knowledge from the inside. "The one who chooses His works" — hairetis: she chooses what He makes, or works beside Him in it (7:22, "the fashioner of all things").

  • v7 "self-control and understanding, righteousness and courage" — sōphrosynē, phronēsis, dikaiosynē, andreia, the four virtues the Greeks counted chief. The book says wisdom teaches all four.

  • v12 "they will put their hands on their mouths" — as the princes did before Job, laid their hand on their mouth (Job 29:9).

  • vv19–20 "a good soul fell to my lot; or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body" — the speaker corrects himself: not a body that was given a soul, but a good self that came into a body.

  • v21 "I would not possess her" — enkratēs, "having mastery," with no object written: of wisdom, or of himself, "self-controlled" (the word of Titus 1:8). "To know whose gift she was" — wisdom is asked for, not earned (James 1:5).

chapters.title: The Prayer for Wisdom
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 9

1God of the fathers and Lord of mercy,
who made all things by Your word,

2and by Your wisdom formed man
to have dominion over the creatures You have made,

3and rule the world in holiness and righteousness,
and pronounce judgment in uprightness of soul,

4give me the wisdom that sits beside Your throne,
and do not reject me from among Your servants.

5For I am Your servant and the son of Your maidservant,
a man who is weak and short-lived,
with little understanding of judgment and laws;

6for even if one is perfect among the sons of men,
without the wisdom that comes from You
he will be counted as nothing.

7You chose me to be king of Your people
and judge of Your sons and daughters.

8You told me to build a temple on Your holy mountain,
and an altar in the city where You dwell,
a copy of the holy tent that You prepared from the beginning.

9With You is wisdom, who knows Your works
and was present when You made the world,
and understands what is pleasing in Your sight
and what is right in Your commandments.

10Send her forth from the holy heavens,
and from the throne of Your glory send her,
so that she may be with me and toil,
and that I may learn what is pleasing to You.

11For she knows and understands all things,
and she will guide me wisely in my actions,
and guard me with her glory.

12Then my works will be acceptable,
and I will judge Your people justly,
and I will be worthy of the throne of my father.

13For what man can know the counsel of God?
Or who can discern what the Lord wills?

14For the reasonings of mortals are timid,
and our designs are likely to fail;

15for a perishable body weighs down the soul,
and this earthly tent burdens the mind full of thoughts.

16We can hardly guess at what is on earth,
and what is at hand we find with labor;
but who has traced out what is in the heavens?

17Who has learned Your counsel,
unless You gave wisdom
and sent Your holy Spirit from on high?

18So the paths of those on earth were set right,
and men were taught what pleases You,
and were saved by wisdom.

Notes

  • vv1–18 — the prayer that 7:7 and 8:21 promised, the prayer at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:6–9; 2 Chronicles 1:8–10) in the book's own words.

  • v1 "who made all things by Your word" — en logō sou: the word by which the heavens were made (Psalm 33:6), and the Word of John 1:3, all things came to be through Him. Here the word and wisdom (v2) stand side by side.

  • v4 "the wisdom that sits beside Your throne" — paredros, "one seated beside," as an assessor sits beside a judge. "Your servants" — paidōn, the word of 2:13 ("a child of the Lord"); here, beside v5, it means those who serve.

  • v5 "I am Your servant and the son of Your maidservant" — the words of Psalm 116:16.

  • v8 "a copy of the holy tent that You prepared from the beginning" — the pattern shown to Moses on the mountain (Exodus 25:9, 40); Hebrews calls the earthly sanctuary a copy and shadow of the heavenly things (Hebrews 8:5).

  • v13 "what man can know the counsel of God?" — Isaiah 40:13; Paul quotes it in Romans 11:34.

  • v15 "this earthly tent burdens the mind" — skēnos, "tent," the body: Paul, while we are still in this tent, we groan, being burdened (2 Corinthians 5:4), uses the same two words.

  • v17 "sent Your holy Spirit from on high" — to hagion sou pneuma, "Your holy Spirit," capital S since it is God's (as in 1:7), and beside wisdom as God's gift (1:5 and its note).

chapters.title: Wisdom in the History of Her People
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 10

1She guarded the first-formed father of the world,
when he alone had been created,
and she delivered him from his own transgression,

2and gave him strength to rule over all things.

3But when an unrighteous man turned away from her in his anger,
he perished in his rage that murdered his brother.

4When the earth was flooded because of him,
wisdom saved it again,
steering the righteous man on a paltry piece of wood.

5She, when the nations in their common wickedness had been confounded,
recognized the righteous man and kept him blameless before God,
and kept him strong against his tenderness for his child.

6She rescued a righteous man when the ungodly were perishing,
as he fled the fire that came down on the Five Cities.

7Evidence of their wickedness still remains:
a smoking wasteland,
plants that bear fruit that never ripens,
and a pillar of salt standing
as a monument to an unbelieving soul.

8For because they passed wisdom by,
they were not only kept from knowing what is good,
but also left the world a reminder of their folly,
so that their failures could not go unnoticed.

9But wisdom rescued from troubles those who served her.

10She, when a righteous man fled from his brother's wrath,
guided him on straight paths;
she showed him the kingdom of God,
and gave him knowledge of holy things;
she prospered him in his hardships,
and made his labors abundant.

11When those who oppressed him were greedy,
she stood by him and made him rich.

12She protected him from his enemies,
and kept him safe from those who lay in wait for him;
in his hard contest she gave him the victory,
so that he might know that godliness is stronger than anything.

13She, when a righteous man was sold, did not abandon him,
but rescued him from sin.

14She went down with him into the pit,
and did not leave him in his chains,
until she brought him the scepter of a kingdom
and authority over those who had lorded it over him;
she showed those who had accused him to be liars,
and gave him everlasting glory.

15She delivered a holy people and a blameless seed
from a nation of oppressors.

16She entered the soul of the Lord's servant,
and withstood dread kings with wonders and signs.

17She gave holy people the reward of their labors;
she guided them along a marvelous way,
and became a shelter for them by day
and a flame of stars through the night.

18She brought them over the Red Sea,
and led them through deep waters;

19but she drowned their enemies,
and cast them up from the depth of the abyss.

20Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly;
they sang, Lord, of Your holy name,
and praised with one accord Your hand that fought for them;

21for wisdom opened the mouths of the mute,
and made the tongues of infants speak clearly.

  • v4 "because of him" — the Flood is laid at Cain's door: the violence that filled the earth (Genesis 6:11) began with his. "A paltry piece of wood" — the ark.

  • v5 "when the nations… had been confounded" — Babel (Genesis 11:9), which comes before Abraham's call. "Against his tenderness for his child" — Isaac on the altar (Genesis 22).

  • vv6–7 "the Five Cities… a pillar of salt" — the cities of the plain (Genesis 14:2), and Lot's wife, who looked back (19:26). "Fruit that never ripens" — atelesin hōrais, fruit whose seasons never come to their end.

  • v10 "she showed him the kingdom of God, and gave him knowledge of holy things" — Jacob at Bethel, the ladder and God above it (Genesis 28:12–17). Hagiōn may also be "holy ones," the messengers on the ladder.

chapters.title: Punished by What They Worshipped
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 11

1She prospered their works by the hand of a holy prophet.

2They journeyed through an uninhabited wilderness,
and pitched their tents in trackless places.

3They stood against their foes,
and fought off their enemies.

4When they were thirsty, they called upon You,
and water was given them out of the flint rock,
and relief from thirst out of hard stone.

5For by the very things through which their enemies were punished,
they themselves were helped in their need.

6Instead of the spring of an ever-flowing river,
stirred up and defiled with blood

7in rebuke for the decree to kill the infants,
You gave them abundant water when they had no hope of it,

8showing by their thirst at that time
how You punished their adversaries.

9For when they were tried,
though they were being disciplined in mercy,
they learned how the ungodly were tormented
when judged in wrath.

10For these You tested as a father does in warning,
but those You examined as a stern king does in condemning.

11Whether absent or present, they were equally distressed,

12for a double grief seized them,
and a groaning at the memory of what had passed.

13For when they heard that through their own punishments
the others had been helped,
they perceived the Lord.

14For the one they had long before cast out and exposed,
and then rejected with scorn,
they marveled at in the end,
when they had thirsted as the righteous had not.

15In return for their foolish and wicked thoughts,
which led them astray to worship
irrational reptiles and worthless creatures,
You sent upon them a multitude of irrational creatures to punish them,

16so that they might learn
that one is punished by the very things by which he sins.

17For Your all-powerful hand,
which created the world out of formless matter,
did not lack the means to send upon them
a multitude of bears or bold lions,

18or newly created beasts, unknown and full of rage,
breathing out a fiery blast,
or puffing out roaring smoke,
or flashing terrible sparks from their eyes,

19whose harm could not only destroy them,
but whose very sight could kill them with fright.

20Even apart from these, they could have fallen at a single breath,
pursued by justice,
and scattered by the breath of Your power.
But You have arranged all things
by measure and number and weight.

21For it is always in Your power to show great strength,
and who can withstand the might of Your arm?

22Because the whole world before You is like a speck that tips the scales,
and like a drop of morning dew that falls on the ground.

23But You have mercy on all, because You can do all things,
and You overlook the sins of men, so that they may repent.

24For You love all things that exist,
and abhor none of the things You have made,
for You would not have made anything if You had hated it.

25How would anything have endured if You had not willed it?
Or how would anything not called by You have been preserved?

26You spare all things, because they are Yours,
Master, lover of life.

Notes

  • v1 "a holy prophet" — Moses, the prophet like no other (Deuteronomy 34:10). From v4 on, the book speaks to God directly, and does so to its end.

  • v4 "out of the flint rock" — Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:11; the Greek of Deuteronomy 8:15 has the same words, ek petras akrotomou.

  • v5 — the rule that governs the rest of the book: the same things that punished Egypt helped Israel. A series of such comparisons runs through chapter 19, beginning here with water: the Nile turned to blood (Exodus 7:20), the rock that gave water.

  • v7 "the decree to kill the infants" — Pharaoh's command that every son be thrown into the Nile (Exodus 1:22): the river that took the children was turned to blood.

  • v10 "as a father… as a stern king" — as a man disciplines his son, the LORD your God disciplines you (Deuteronomy 8:5).

  • v14 "the one they had long before cast out and exposed" — Moses, set out on the Nile as a baby (Exodus 2:3) and later rejected (2:14).

  • vv15–16 "one is punished by the very things by which he sins" — Egypt worshipped animals, and was struck by frogs, gnats, flies and locusts.

  • v20 "by measure and number and weight" — compare Job 28:25 and Isaiah 40:12. "The breath of Your power" — a blast of God's breath, lowercase here as a wind that scatters (5:23), as in Isaiah 11:4, with the breath of his lips he shall kill the wicked.

  • v22 "like a speck that tips the scales" — Isaiah 40:15, the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are counted as the dust on the scales.

  • v26 "Master, lover of life" — Despota philopsyche, "lover of souls": the God who made all things spares them because they are His.

chapters.title: Little by Little
chapters.html:
Wisdom of Solomon 12

1For Your incorruptible Spirit is in all things.

2Therefore You correct little by little those who go astray,
and You remind and warn them of the things by which they sin,
so that they may be freed from wickedness
and believe in You, Lord.

3For the old inhabitants of Your holy land

4You hated for their most hateful practices,
their works of sorcery and unholy rites,

5their merciless slaughter of children,
their feasting on human flesh and blood,
initiates from among a frenzied band,

6parents who murdered helpless souls —
these You willed to destroy by the hands of our fathers,

7so that the land most precious of all to You
might receive a worthy colony of the children of God.

8Yet even these You spared, since they were men,
and sent hornets as forerunners of Your army,
to destroy them little by little,

9though You were not unable to give the ungodly
into the hands of the righteous in battle,
or to destroy them at one blow
by dread wild beasts or a stern word.

10But judging them little by little, You gave them a place for repentance,
though You knew that their origin was evil
and their wickedness inborn,
and that their way of thinking would never change.

11For they were a seed accursed from the beginning;
nor was it out of fear of anyone
that You left them unpunished for their sins.

12For who will say, "What have You done?"
Or who will resist Your judgment?
Who will accuse You for the destruction of nations that You made?
Or who will come before You to plead as an avenger
for unrighteous men?

13For there is no god besides You,
whose care is for all,
to whom You must show that You have not judged unjustly;

14nor can any king or monarch confront You
about those whom You have punished.

15You are righteous and rule all things righteously,
counting it foreign to Your power
to condemn one who does not deserve to be punished.

16For Your strength is the source of righteousness,
and because You are Master of all, You spare all.

17For You show Your strength
when men doubt that Your power is complete,
and among those who know it, You rebuke their insolence.

18But You, who are master of strength, judge with gentleness,
and with great forbearance You govern us;
for You have power to act whenever You choose.

19Through such works You have taught Your people
that the righteous man must love mankind,
and You have made Your sons full of good hope,
because You give repentance for sins.

20For if You punished the enemies of Your children,
who deserved to die,
with such great care and pleading,
granting them time and opportunity
to be freed from their wickedness,

21with what strictness You have judged Your sons,
to whose fathers You gave oaths and covenants
full of good promises!

22So while You discipline us,
You scourge our enemies ten thousand times more,
so that when we judge, we may think of Your goodness,
and when we are judged, we may expect mercy.

23Therefore those who lived unrighteously, in the folly of their life,
You tormented through their own detestable things.

24For they went far astray on the paths of error,
taking for gods those animals
that even their enemies despised,
deceived like foolish infants.

25Therefore, as to children who cannot reason,
You sent Your judgment to mock them.

26But those who would not be warned by mocking rebukes
will experience a judgment worthy of God.

27For when they suffered, they were indignant at the creatures
they had thought to be gods,
and were punished by means of them;
and they saw and recognized as the true God
Him whom they had long refused to know.
Therefore the last of condemnation came upon them.

Notes

  • v1 "Your incorruptible Spirit is in all things" — to aphtharton sou pneuma, capital S since it is God's (as 1:7 and 9:17): the Spirit that fills the world (1:7) holds every creature in being, and so God spares what He made (11:24–26).

  • vv3–7 "the old inhabitants of Your holy land" — the Canaanites; the practices listed are those Deuteronomy names as the reason for their removal (Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:9–12).

  • v5 "initiates from among a frenzied band" — ek mesou mystas thiasou: thiasos is a band of worshippers in an ecstatic rite. The Greek of the line is uneven, and its exact sense uncertain.

  • v7 "the children of God" — theou paidōn; pais is "child" or "servant" (2:13; 9:4). Here, beside "Your sons" (vv19, 21), it is "children."

  • v8 "hornets as forerunners of Your army" — I will send the hornet before you (Exodus 23:28; Deuteronomy 7:20; Joshua 24:12).

  • v10 "a place for repentance" — topon metanoias, the phrase of Hebrews 12:17, where Esau found no place for repentance.

  • v11 "a seed accursed from the beginning" — Cursed be Canaan (Genesis 9:25).

  • v12 "who will say, 'What have You done?'" — Job 9:12; Ecclesiastes 8:4; Paul, who are you, man, to answer back to God? (Romans 9:20).

  • v19 "the righteous man must love mankind" — philanthrōpon, the word used of wisdom's own spirit (1:6; 7:23): God's patience teaches His people to be like Him.

  • v20 "with such great care and pleading" — deēsis, "entreaty": even God's punishment of Canaan came with a call to turn.
